instruction: Identify the community discussion topic with the top number of responses and open it.

metadata.explanation: Task requires identifying and accessing the discussion with the highest response count. Evaluator checks for successful URL navigation.

llm_judge_reasons: Critical semantic flaw: The expected URL is hardcoded as 'https://discussions.flightaware.com/t/the-banter-thread/4412' but the instruction requires identifying 'the community discussion topic with the top number of responses'
The 'top discussion by response count' is dynamic and can change over time as users add responses to different topics, but the evaluator uses a static expected URL
The evaluator cannot verify that the agent correctly IDENTIFIED the top discussion - it only checks if a specific hardcoded URL was opened

Incomplete verification: The instruction has two requirements (identify top discussion + open it), but the evaluator only verifies the second step (opening a URL) without verifying the identification logic

At evaluation time, if the actual top discussion is a different topic (e.g., a different thread has more responses now), the evaluator will incorrectly fail even if the agent correctly identified and opened the real top discussion
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: The evaluator should dynamically scrape the FlightAware discussions page to identify which topic actually has the most responses at evaluation time
Use a getter that extracts discussion metadata (topic titles and response counts) from the discussions listing page
Compare the opened URL against the dynamically-identified top discussion URL, not a hardcoded static URL
Alternative: Add a getter that parses the opened discussion page to extract its response count, then verify this count is the maximum among all discussions (requires scraping all discussion counts)
Consider adding metadata about when the expected URL was verified to be the top discussion, and flag tasks that may have stale expected values
